sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

My review of C1 (I verified the backend myself on this machine; reproduce and record these probes):
- engines = ['qnnpack']. torch.ao.quantization.quantize_dynamic works and yields native
  torch.ao.nn.quantized.dynamic Linear modules. FX static (prepare_fx/convert_fx with
  get_default_qconfig_mapping("qnnpack"), calibrate, convert) works and yields native LinearReLU /
  quantized modules. torch.ao.quantization.quantize_pt2e does NOT exist; torchao is not installed.
  nn.Linear runs natively in float16 and bfloat16 on CPU (output dtype stays fp16/bf16).
- OVERRULED: QuantLinear8 / QuantConv8 in precision.py compute INT8 with hand-written int64 matmuls in
  Python. That is an emulation, not the backend's INT8 kernel, so its latency is meaningless as "INT8 on
  this laptop". Remove them from the INT8 path. INT8 rows must use the native modules:
  dynamic = quantize_dynamic({nn.Linear}, qint8); static = FX prepare_fx/convert_fx with the qnnpack
  qconfig mapping, calibrated per C.1. Conv2d static INT8 via FX on qnnpack: try it; if the backend
  rejects it, record a classified unsupported row and leave conv in fp32 (counted in frac_macs).
- GCN: GCNConv/propagate is not FX-quantizable. Quantize only the projection by swapping each
  conv.lin for an nn.Linear with identical weights (verify logits equal before quantizing), then apply
  dynamic / static to those Linears; aggregation stays fp32 and is counted as fp32 MACs. If that fails,
  classified unsupported row.
- BUG: the C1 fp16 rows score 5-15% (chance). A correct fp16 cast loses < 0.5 pp. Find and fix the cause
  (check the checkpoint is loaded, the input is normalized exactly as in eval, and both model and input
  are cast). Add a test: fp16 and bf16 val accuracy within 1 pp of fp32 for all three architectures.
- BUG: precision.py loads splits via RESULTS_DIR.parent / "splits", which breaks when tests redirect
  LAB3_RESULTS_DIR. Use the project root, as the rest of the package does.
- The 15 part="C" rows already in runs.jsonl are C1 development/debug rows: list their run_ids in
  results/ANNOTATIONS.md as "C1 debug — excluded"; move the matching files in results/precision_artifacts/
  into _quarantine/c1_debug/. Never edit runs.jsonl.
- INT4 simulated weight-only (Int4Packed*) is fine to keep as long as it is labelled
  simulated_non_native and follows C.1 (per-output-channel symmetric [-8,7], fp32 scales, 2 per uint8).

Then complete the original C1 task items 1-9 exactly as written in transcripts/prompts/C1_precision.md
(support report with probe evidence, all conversions for all 3 archs with the full accounting fields,
reload-equivalence, tests, INT8 selection by the frozen rule, the 12-condition factorial, figures,
partc_summary.md). Write real records with phase "precision" / "factorial".

Final item — Part B figure cleanup (scripts/make_figures.py only, no data changes): the three Part B
figures render with an EMPTY band where the shared legend should be (fig.legend is not drawing — likely

# Lab 3 — Predictions and Frozen Design Decisions

Each section is dated and was written **before** the runs it governs. Sections are
append-only: later corrections are added as dated amendments, never by editing a frozen
section.

---

## Part A — Dense reference models (frozen 2026-11-09, before any training)

### A.1 Frozen design

**Hardware / software.** Apple M4 Pro (12 CPU cores), 24 GB RAM, macOS. Python 3.12,
PyTorch 2.15.0, torchvision 0.29.2, torch_geometric 2.8.1, NumPy 2.5.4. Package
management with `uv` (`pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`). **CPU only for every arm**; no MPS.

**Threads.** `torch.set_num_threads(4)` and `torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)` for all
training, evaluation, and benchmarking.

**Data splits (created once, saved to `splits/`, reused by every arm).**
- Fashion-MNIST: official 60k train / 10k test. From the 60k train set, a stratified
  5,000-image validation set (500 per class) is drawn once with split seed 12345; the
  remaining 55,000 images are the training set. The 10k official test set is the test set.
  Saved as index files plus a SHA-256 of the index arrays.
- Cora: the standard Planetoid public split (140 train / 500 val / 1000 test nodes), saved
  as node-index files with a SHA-256. The graph (2,708 nodes, 10,556 directed edges) is
  never modified by any compression arm.
- Inputs: Fashion-MNIST normalized with mean/std computed on the 55k training split only.
  Cora features row-normalized (standard GCN preprocessing).

**Architectures.**
| Model | Definition | Params (computed) |
|---|---|---|
| MLP | 784→256→128→10, ReLU, no dropout | 235,146 |
| CNN | Conv(1→16, 5×5, pad 2)→ReLU→MaxPool2 → Conv(16→32, 5×5)→ReLU→MaxPool2 → FC(800→128)→ReLU → FC(128→10) | 117,066 |
| GCN | GCNConv(1433→16)→ReLU→Dropout(0.5) → GCNConv(16→7) | 23,063 |

No BatchNorm anywhere (keeps INT8 conversion and structured surgery unambiguous).

**Training.**
- MLP and CNN: Adam, lr 1e-3, weight decay 0, batch size 128, cross-entropy, max **30
  epochs**.
- GCN: Adam, lr 0.01, weight decay 5e-4, full-batch, cross-entropy on the 140 train nodes,
  max **300 epochs**.

**Early stopping / checkpoint selection (validation only).** After each epoch, evaluate
validation accuracy. Keep the checkpoint with the highest validation accuracy; ties go to
the lower validation loss, then to the earlier epoch. Stop when validation accuracy has not
improved for **5 epochs** (MLP, CNN) or **50 epochs** (GCN), or at the max epoch count. The
test set is evaluated only on the selected checkpoint and never feeds back into any choice.

**Seeds.** Each run sets Python `random`, NumPy, and PyTorch seeds to the run seed and logs
it.
- Pilot seed: **0**. Produces the canonical dense checkpoint per architecture. Every
  compression arm starts from it, and the full Part B pilot matrix uses it.
- Confirmatory seeds: **1, 2, 3**. Used (a) to train three replica dense baselines per
  architecture, which report seed variance only and are never used as compression parents,
  and (b) in Part B to repeat the selected operating points. There the seed controls
  fine-tuning shuffle order and dropout, and the parent is always the canonical seed-0
  checkpoint.
- The split seed 12345 is separate from these and is never changed.

**Sanity targets (test accuracy).** MLP ≥ 82%, CNN ≥ 87%, GCN ≥ 65%. A miss is diagnosed,
and the cause is recorded. The target is not lowered.

**Latency protocol.** `torch.inference_mode()`, model in `eval()`. 20 warm-up and 200
timed iterations, timed with `time.perf_counter_ns`. Report the median and IQR. Batch sizes
are **1** and **256** for Fashion-MNIST, and one full-graph forward pass for Cora. Peak RSS
is measured in a fresh subprocess per benchmark.

**Stopping rule for agent work.** If a baseline misses its target after one diagnosed fix,
or any required test fails twice after a fix, work stops and the issue is reviewed before
continuing. Tests are never weakened to pass.

### A.2 Predictions

**Parameter count: MLP (235k) > CNN (117k) > GCN (23k).**
*Mechanism:* the MLP's first layer alone (784×256 ≈ 201k) dominates its count. The CNN
shares 5×5 kernels across positions, so its convolutions are tiny (≈13k), and most of its
parameters sit in FC(800→128) (≈103k). The GCN has a 16-wide hidden layer, so nearly all
of its parameters are the 1433×16 input projection.

**Dense checkpoint size: MLP (~0.94 MB) > CNN (~0.47 MB) > GCN (~0.09 MB).**
*Mechanism:* FP32 state dicts are about 4 bytes × params, plus a few KB of pickle/zip
overhead. The overhead is proportionally largest for the GCN, so its ratio to the others
will be slightly above the raw parameter ratio. The Cora graph is data, not checkpoint.

**Training time to the selected checkpoint: CNN > MLP > GCN.**
*Mechanism:* per image, the CNN does about 1.7M MACs (conv2 alone is about 1.28M), against
0.235M for the MLP. That is about 7× more compute over the same 55k images per epoch,
partly offset by better-optimized conv kernels. The GCN trains full-batch on 2,708 nodes.
Each epoch is one sparse aggregation plus a 2708×1433×16 projection, so 300 epochs should
take seconds, against minutes for the image models.

**Sensitivity to compression (most to least): GCN > CNN > MLP.**
*Mechanism:*
- *GCN:* it has a 16-dimensional bottleneck and only 140 labelled nodes for fine-tuning.
  Every remaining weight carries a large share of the representation, and recovery data is
  scarce. Most of its input-projection weights belong to rare bag-of-words features, so
  moderate unstructured sparsity should be tolerated. At high sparsity, and for structured
  removal of hidden features, I expect the sharpest collapse.
- *CNN:* convolution weights are reused at every spatial position, so pruning one conv
  weight perturbs many activations. Global magnitude pruning should mostly remove FC
  weights, which buffers it, but structured channel pruning of a 16/32-channel network
  should hurt.
- *MLP:* it is heavily over-parameterized for Fashion-MNIST. Many first-layer weights
  attach to border pixels with near-constant input, so they carry little signal and should
  prune almost for free up to high sparsity.
- *Precision:* I predict INT8 costs every model < 0.5 pp of accuracy. Simulated INT4 should
  hurt the GCN and CNN more than the MLP, for the same bottleneck and weight-reuse reasons.

**Expected baseline test accuracy:** MLP about 88–89%, CNN about 90–91%, GCN about 80–81%.

---

## Part B — Four forms of sparsity (frozen 2026-11-09, before any pruning run)

### B.1 Common protocol (all four methods)

- **Parent:** every arm starts from the canonical seed-0 dense checkpoint of its
  architecture (`checkpoints/dense/<arch>_seed0.pt`).
- **One-shot pruning,** followed by a fixed fine-tuning budget. There is no iterative
  pruning.
- **Eligible tensors:** the weight matrix/kernel of every Linear, Conv2d, and GCNConv layer,
  including the final classifier. Biases are never pruned, and there are no normalization
  layers.
- **Fine-tuning budget (identical for every method within an architecture):**
  - MLP/CNN: 3 epochs, Adam lr 5e-4, batch 128, frozen 55k training split.
  - GCN: 50 epochs, Adam lr 0.005, weight decay 5e-4, dropout 0.5, 140 training nodes.
  - The fine-tuning checkpoint is the epoch with the best validation accuracy inside that
    budget. Ties go to the later epoch, which is the more-trained model.
- **Masks:** for S1/S3/S4 a binary mask is re-applied after every optimizer step, so pruned
  entries stay exactly zero. Adam state for masked entries is irrelevant because the mask
  is applied to the weights.
- **Measurement stages:** every arm is measured twice: immediately after pruning, before
  any update (`stage=post_prune`), and after fine-tuning (`stage=post_finetune`). Both rows
  carry val/test accuracy, per-layer sparsity, bytes, MACs, latency, and memory.
- **Pilot:** seed 0 for the full 3 × 4 × 4 matrix. In fine-tuning, the seed controls data
  order and dropout.
- **Calibration subset (S3 now, reused in Part C):**
  - Fashion-MNIST: 1,024 images from the **training** split, stratified 102–103 per class,
    drawn once with seed 12345 and saved to `splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy`. The labels are
    training labels.
  - Cora: the 140 training nodes on the full graph.
  - No validation or test labels are ever used for calibration.

### B.2 Method specifications

**S1 Global unstructured magnitude.** Pool all eligible weights across layers, then zero
the fraction *s* with the smallest |w|. Targets: 25/50/75/90%. Achieved sparsity is
reported globally and per tensor.

**S2 Structured group pruning (L1).** Groups and their L1 norms:
- MLP: hidden units of both hidden layers. The norm is the unit's incoming weight row.
- CNN: output channels of conv1 and conv2 (L1 of each filter) and FC1 hidden units.
  Removing conv2 channels also removes the matching FC1 input columns.
- GCN: the 16 hidden features. The norm is the incoming weight column of layer 1.

Ranking is **layer-wise**: each prunable layer removes the same fraction, keeping
k = max(1, round((1 − s)·n)) groups. The classifier output and the input dimension are
never pruned. The model is **physically rebuilt** as a smaller dense model by copying the
surviving rows/columns/bias entries. The target is the fraction of groups removed, and the
achieved value is reported as both group sparsity and parameter sparsity relative to the
dense model. These differ. For example, at s = 90%, GCN keeps round(1.6) = 2 features, so
87.5% of groups are removed.

**S3 First-order saliency (unstructured, global; this choice is fixed).** The score is
|w ⊙ ∂L/∂w|, where L is the mean cross-entropy over the whole calibration subset (one
gradient computed on the dense parent in eval mode, so no dropout). Pool all eligible
weights across layers and zero the lowest-scoring fraction *s*.

**S4 N:M semi-structured.**
- Blocks are M consecutive weights along each row's **reduction (input) dimension**. Conv
  kernels are flattened to [out, in·k·k]. In each block, keep the N largest |w|.
- If the row length is not divisible by M, the final partial block of length r keeps
  ⌈N·r/M⌉ weights.
- **Patterns, chosen before running:** 3:4 (25%), 2:4 (50%), 1:4 (75%), and 1:10 (90%,
  following the instructor's guidance). Every pilot cell is filled by a real run.
- Partial blocks make achieved sparsity slightly below the nominal value for rows with
  remainders: conv1 rows have 25 weights, and GCN layer 1 rows have 1,433. Achieved
  sparsity is reported.
- No cell is filled by copying another run.

### B.3 Confirmatory point selection rule (validation only; fixed before any test result is seen)

For each architecture × method, take the pilot (seed 0) post-fine-tune rows:

1. **Eligible levels:** post-fine-tune validation accuracy ≥ dense seed-0 validation
   accuracy − τ. τ = 1.0 pp for MLP and CNN. τ = 2.0 pp for GCN, whose 500-node validation
   set gives one node = 0.2 pp and a binomial SE of ~1.8 pp.
2. **Choose** the eligible level with the **highest target sparsity**.
3. **Fallback:** if no level is eligible, choose the level with the highest post-fine-tune
   validation accuracy. Ties go to the lower sparsity.
4. **Rerun** the chosen point with seeds 1, 2, 3, using the same parent and budget.

Test accuracy is logged but never read by this rule.

### B.4 Two runtime paths

- **Path 1:** dense PyTorch modules holding zero-valued weights. Run this for every arm.
- **Path 2: genuinely compact export.**
  - S2: the physically rebuilt dense model.
  - S1/S3: `torch.sparse_csr` weights executed with sparse matmul (sparse × dense), plus
    a CSR file on disk.
  - S4: a packed N:M file (kept values + a small index per kept value) for size.
- If the CPU backend has no semi-structured kernel, S4 runtime is recorded as unsupported
  or dense-fallback. It is never inferred from the zero count.

### B.5 Predictions (per method)

**S1 global magnitude.**
- *(i) Largest loss at 75%:* **GCN**, about −1 pp after fine-tuning. It has the smallest
  network and the least labelled data for recovery. Before fine-tuning I expect MLP ≈ −1,
  CNN ≈ −2, and GCN ≈ −3 pp.
- *(ii) Recovery:* fine-tuning recovers almost all loss up to 75%. At 90% it recovers most,
  leaving MLP/CNN about 1–2 pp and GCN about 3–5 pp below dense.
- *(iii) Size and runtime:*
  - The dense-path file size and latency will **not** change, because zeros are stored and
    multiplied as FP32. Gzip will shrink the file roughly with sparsity.
  - CSR export becomes smaller than dense only above roughly 60–67% sparsity, since each
    nonzero costs 4 B of value plus an 8 B int64 column index.
  - Sparse matmul will be **slower** than dense at every level for these small layers,
    including 90%.

**S2 structured.**
- *(i) Largest loss at 75%:* **CNN before fine-tuning.** It drops to 4 and 8 channels and
  each removed channel loses a whole feature map, so I expect a drop of tens of pp.
  **GCN after fine-tuning:** 4 hidden features for 7 classes is a bottleneck narrower than
  the class count, and I expect −5 to −10 pp.
- *(ii) Recovery:* fine-tuning recovers most of the loss for MLP/CNN, leaving them 1–3 pp
  below dense at 75%. It recovers less for GCN.
- *(iii) Size and runtime:* the only method with **real** dense-path reductions.
  - File size shrinks roughly with parameters.
  - At batch 256, MLP/CNN latency falls roughly with MACs.
  - At batch 1, latency is dominated by framework overhead (~10 µs), so the speedup is
    small.
  - GCN latency falls modestly because the X·W projection shrinks, while aggregation and
    overhead remain.

**S3 saliency (unstructured).**
- *(i) Largest loss at 75%:* **GCN**. Its post-prune accuracy should be slightly better than
  S1 at 50–75% because the score accounts for the gradient. At 90%, a gradient taken at a
  near-converged dense point is noisy, so I expect it to be no better than S1.
- *(ii) Recovery:* similar to S1.
- *(iii) Size and runtime:* same as S1, since it produces the same unstructured format.

**S4 N:M.**
- *(i) Largest loss at 75% (1:4):* **CNN** before fine-tuning. The local per-block
  constraint is harsher than global ranking, and conv1 has only 25 weights per filter.
  After fine-tuning, the GCN loses the most.
- *(ii) Recovery:* 3:4 and 2:4 recover to within about 0.5 pp. 1:4 and 1:10 lose more than
  S1 at the same sparsity, because the pattern can't concentrate surviving weights in the
  important rows.
- *(iii) Size and runtime:*
  - I predict **no runtime gain** on this laptop, because PyTorch has no semi-structured
    sparse CPU kernel on ARM. Expect a dense fallback.
  - The packed N:M file will be smaller than dense at 2:4 and sparser levels.
  - Dense-path file size is unchanged.

**Cross-method expectation:** for deployment on this laptop, only S2 will improve both size
and measured latency. S1/S3/S4 will mainly show that more zeros ≠ faster.

## Part C — Reduced precision (frozen 2026-11-09, before any Part C run)

### C.1 Frozen design

**Parents.** The standalone precision study starts from the canonical seed-0 dense FP32
checkpoint of each architecture. Conversion is post-training only; there is no QAT.

**Formats.** Each one is run only where the laptop backend supports it. An unsupported
format gets a classified failed/unsupported row, never a missing cell.
1. **FP16 and BF16.** Weights and inputs are cast. I will report whether each op actually
   executes in that dtype on CPU, and any upcasting, by inspecting output dtypes per layer
   and checking kernel support.
2. **Dynamic INT8.** INT8 weights with per-batch activation quantization, applied to
   Linear-type layers, on whichever quantized engine is available (`qnnpack` was the only
   engine at setup). GCN projections are included if the backend can quantize them,
   otherwise they are classified as unsupported.
3. **Static INT8 (calibrated).** INT8 weights and activations with observers calibrated on
   the subset below. It uses whichever supported flow works, and records which flow was used
   (eager, FX, or PT2E). Ops that cannot be quantized stay FP32, and are counted as such.
4. **Simulated weight-only INT4.**
   - Per-output-channel symmetric quantization to [−8, 7], with an FP32 scale per output
     channel.
   - Two values are packed per uint8 on disk.
   - At runtime the weights are dequantized to FP32 and computed in FP32. This is
     **labelled simulated/non-native**, and the dequantization cost is either inside or
     outside the timed region. That choice is recorded and applied identically everywhere.

**Required accounting per row.**
- Stored, compute, and accumulator precision.
- Actual serialized bytes on disk.
- The **fraction of MACs that truly executed in reduced precision**, computed from the
  per-layer MAC table and which layers actually ran quantized/half kernels.
- Reload equivalence: logits of the reloaded artifact vs the in-memory converted model,
  within an explicit tolerance. The tolerance is 0 for exact formats, and 1e-5 relative for
  FP32 recompute paths.

**Calibration rule (frozen).**
- Fashion-MNIST: the same 1,024-image calibration subset as S3. It comes from the
  **training** split, stratified 102–103 per class, seed 12345, saved as
  `splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy`. Only inputs are used, no labels.
- Cora: the single full-graph forward pass over all node features with the fixed graph.
  This is inputs only. No labels of any split are used, and it is the only coherent
  calibration for a transductive full-graph model.
- No validation or test labels are used anywhere in calibration.

**Best supported INT8 method per architecture (frozen rule).** Among dynamic and static
INT8 conversions of the dense parent that are supported for that architecture, choose the
one with the **higher validation accuracy**. Ties within one validation example go to the
lower batch-256 / full-graph median latency. If only one method is supported, use it.

**Sparse operating point per architecture (frozen rule, validation-based; applied after
the Part B confirmations, before any Part C run).**
- Consider the four confirmed Part B points (S1–S4) for that architecture.
- *Eligible:* mean post-fine-tune validation accuracy over confirmatory seeds 1–3 must be
  ≥ dense seed-0 validation − τ, counted in correct validation examples, with τ as in B.3.
- Among the eligible points, choose the one with the **smallest measured serialized size of
  its best compact artifact** (CSR for S1/S3, the rebuilt model for S2, the N:M pack for
  S4). This is the smallest deployable model that keeps validation accuracy. Size is a
  property of the artifact, not of test data.
- Ties within 1% of bytes go to the higher mean validation accuracy.
- If none is eligible, choose the point with the highest mean validation accuracy.
- The chosen point's **seed-0 pilot checkpoint** is the sparse FP32 parent for the
  factorial.

**Factorial (12 conditions).**
- For each architecture: dense FP32, sparse FP32, dense INT8, and sparse+INT8 (the best
  INT8 method above, applied to the sparse model).
- For mask-based sparsity I report whether zeros survive quantization (the nonzero count
  after INT8), the INT8 file size, and, where implementable, a sparse-INT8 storage size.
  The latter is labelled as runtime-unsupported if there is no sparse INT8 kernel.

### C.2 Predictions

**Format that minimizes file size: simulated INT4.** It stores about 0.5 B/weight plus one
FP32 scale per output channel, so files will be about 13–14% of FP32 for MLP/CNN. The GCN
will be slightly worse because its container overhead is proportionally larger. INT8 comes
second at about 26–28% of FP32, and FP16/BF16 at about 50%.

**Format that minimizes latency: none of the reduced formats beats FP32 at batch 1 on any
model.**
- At batch 256 I expect at most a modest INT8 gain on the MLP (dynamic) and possibly the CNN
  (static, if conv runs on qnnpack).
- FP16/BF16 will be *slower* than or equal to FP32 on this CPU, because of weak half-precision
  CPU kernels and casts.
- Simulated INT4 will be the slowest, because it pays dequantization and still computes in
  FP32.
- For the GCN, the full-graph sparse aggregation is not quantized, and the X·W projection
  stays FP32 or gets converted at a cost. I expect no reduced-precision speedup.

**Why the size winner and the latency winner need not be the same.** File size is set only
by the bits stored per weight. Latency is set by whether the backend has a **native kernel**
that computes in that dtype, plus conversion overheads: quantizing and dequantizing
activations, casts, and layout packing. For models this small, fixed dispatch overhead
dominates arithmetic. INT4 has the smallest footprint but no native compute here, so it is
the opposite of fastest.

**Accuracy.**
- FP16/BF16: < 0.1 pp change; BF16 possibly up to 0.3 pp.
- Dynamic INT8: < 0.3 pp.
- Static INT8: < 0.5 pp.
- INT4: MLP −0.5 to −1 pp, CNN −1 to −2 pp, GCN −1 to −3 pp.
- Ranking of sensitivity to precision: GCN ≥ CNN > MLP.

**Composition.**
- *Size:* sizes compose only when the sparse format carries INT8 values. With int32 indices,
  index overhead dominates, so sparse+INT8 storage beats dense INT8 only at high sparsity
  (about ≥ 80%).
- *Latency:* latency will **not** compose. There is no sparse INT8 CPU kernel, so
  sparse+INT8 runs as dense INT8 with zeros, at the same latency as dense INT8.
- *Accuracy:* the loss will be roughly additive, and small.
- *Zeros:* zeros survive symmetric INT8 weight quantization exactly, because 0 maps to 0.

  2.15 the public `tq.convert` path does not consult the qnnpack engine for

  top level). It is therefore unusable as-is; we drive `QLinear.from_float` /

* FX `prepare_fx/convert_fx` exist (deprecated; require qconfig_mapping +

* PT2E (`torch.ao.quantization.quantize_pt2e`) does not exist in torch 2.15
  (moved to torchao, which is NOT installed; not added — not needed).
* fp16/bf16: `nn.Linear` and `nn.Conv2d` execute natively in fp16/bf16 on CPU
  (output dtype == input dtype; no upcast); no upcasting observed.
* GCNConv: the PyG wrapper (gcn_norm / propagate / scatter) has no quantized or
  half-precision kernel in this build; only its inner projection `GCNConv.lin`
  (an `nn.Linear`) can run reduced precision. Reduced-precision GCN rows
  therefore record that the projection ran reduced precision and the
  aggregation/normalization ran fp32.

INT8 method (eager qnnpack flow):
- Weights are quantized per output channel (symmetric qint8) — qnnpack's
  per-channel scheme; biases kept in fp32; outputs dequantized to fp32.
- Dynamic: activation scale/zero-point computed per batch (per tensor,
  unsigned 8-bit, max |a| / 127 convention).
- Static: activation qparams calibrated on the frozen calibration inputs only
  (1,024 fmnist training images, `splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy`; Cora full
  graph). We run `tq.prepare` (observer) on a copy of the layer, feed the
  calibration inputs through it (activations only), then `Q*.from_float`.

  `HistogramObserver(reduce_range=False)` (qnnpack default qconfig) — its

Simulated weight-only INT4 (frozen C.1):
- Per-output-channel symmetric quantization to [-8, 7], fp32 scale per output

- Dequantize to fp32 and compute in fp32. **The dequantization is INSIDE the
  timed region** (decided once, applied identically to every INT4 run): the
  benchmarked module holds only the packed uint8 weights + fp32 scales and
  rebuilds the fp32 weight each forward (cached until the packed buffer

def set_qnnpack_engine() -> None:
    """Enable the qnnpack quantized engine (the only one on this machine)."""
    torch.backends.quantized.engine = "qnnpack"
    assert torch._C._get_qengine() == 2  # QNNPACK


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Eligible weight-bearing ops
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def eligible_ops(model: nn.Module) -> list[tuple[str, nn.Module, str]]:
    """(name, module, kind) for every Linear / Conv2d / GCNConv projection.

    kind: 'linear' (nn.Linear), 'conv' (nn.Conv2d), 'lin' (GCNConv's inner
    nn.Linear projection, state key <name>.lin). GCNConv itself is never
    reduced-precision-capable on this backend; only its .lin is."""
    out = []
    for name, mod in model.named_modules():
        t = type(mod).__name__
        if t == "Linear":
            out.append((name, mod, "linear"))
        elif t == "Conv2d":
            out.append((name, mod, "conv"))
        elif t == "GCNConv":
            out.append((f"{name}.lin", mod.lin, "lin"))
    return out


def weight_of(mod: nn.Module) -> nn.Parameter:
    return mod.lin.weight if type(mod).__name__ == "GCNConv" else mod.weight


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Forward hooks (output-dtype inspection + reduced-precision MAC accounting)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

REDUCED_DTYPES = {torch.float16, torch.bfloat16}


def inspect_forwards(model, arch: str, iters: int = 3) -> dict[str, torch.dtype]:
    """Run `iters` eval-mode forwards on the fixed bench input and record the
    ACTUAL output dtype of every eligible op (evidence for the support report
    and the per-layer compute-precision table)."""
    set_threads()
    x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
    seen: dict[str, torch.dtype] = {}
    hooks = []
    for name, _, _ in eligible_ops(model):
        def _hook(n=name):
            def h(m, inp, out):
                seen[n] = out.dtype
            return h
        mod = dict(model.named_modules())[name]
        hooks.append(mod.register_forward_hook(_hook()))
    model.eval()
    in_dtype = _model_in_dtype(model)
    try:
        clear_gcn_caches(model)
        with torch.inference_mode():
            for _ in range(iters):
                if arch == "gcn":
                    model(x.to(in_dtype), ei)
                else:
                    model(x[:8].to(in_dtype))
    finally:
        for h in hooks:
            h.remove()
    return seen


def _model_in_dtype(model: nn.Module) -> torch.dtype:
    """Input dtype the converted model expects: fp16/bf16 for half models,
    fp32 for fp32/INT8-wrapper/INT4 models."""
    for m in model.modules():
        if isinstance(m, (QuantLinear8, QuantConv8, Int4PackedLinear, Int4PackedConv)):
            return torch.float32
    for p in model.parameters():
        if p.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
            return p.dtype
    return torch.float32


def _weight_macs(model, x, ei) -> list[dict]:
    """Per-eligible-op MAC table (same conventions as bench.estimate_macs):
    per-image for fmnist (per-token linear / per-pixel conv), full graph for
    GCN (projection N*in*out + aggregation (E+N)*out per layer)."""
    from .bench import _mac_entries

    in_dtype = _model_in_dtype(model)
    entries = _mac_entries(model, (x[:1].to(in_dtype) if ei is None else x.to(in_dtype)), ei)
    is_gcn = ei is not None
    if is_gcn:
        N = int(x.shape[0])
        E_plus_N = int(ei.shape[1]) + N
    table = []
    for e in entries:
        if e["type"] == "GCNConv":
            name = e["name"] + ".lin"  # the reduced-precision unit is the projection
            macs = e["numel"] * e["tokens"] + E_plus_N * e["out_ch"]
        else:
            name = e["name"]
            macs = e["numel"] * e["tokens"]
        table.append({"name": name, "type": e["type"], "macs": int(macs),
                      "nnz": e["nnz"], "numel": e["numel"]})
    return table


def frac_macs_reduced_precision(model, arch: str, reduced_layer_names: set[str]) -> float:
    """Fraction of total MACs performed by ops whose recorded output dtype (or
    explicit quantized status) shows reduced-precision execution.
    fp32 -> 0.0; every eligible op reduced -> 1.0."""
    x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
    table = _weight_macs(model, x, ei)
    total = sum(t["macs"] for t in table)
    if total == 0:
        return 0.0
    red = sum(t["macs"] for t in table if t["name"] in reduced_layer_names)
    return red / total

def calibration_inputs(arch: str):
    """Frozen calibration inputs. fmnist: the 1,024 training-split images in
    splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy (asserted subset of the train split, inputs
    only, normalized identically to training). Cora: the full-graph features
    (the only coherent transductive calibration; inputs only)."""
    if arch == "gcn":
        data = load_cora()
        return {"x": data.x.contiguous(), "edge_index": data.edge_index,
                "n": int(data.x.shape[0]), "rule": "Cora full-graph features only"}
    idx = np.load(CALIB_FILE)
    train_idx = np.load(RESULTS_DIR.parent / "splits" / "fmnist_train_idx.npy")
    assert set(int(i) for i in idx).issubset(set(int(i) for i in train_idx)), \
        "calib idx must be a subset of the train split"
    tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, mean, std = fmnist_split_tensors()
    calib = tr_x[idx.astype(np.int64)].contiguous()
    return {"x": calib, "n": int(calib.shape[0]),
            "rule": "splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy (1024 train-split images, inputs only)"}


def _calib_batch_fn(calib: dict, arch: str):
    """Generator of calibration batches through which a PREPARED (observer)
    model is run. fmnist: 64-image batches (activations quantized per batch).
    Cora: a single full-graph pass."""
    if arch == "gcn":
        def once(model):
            model(calib["x"], calib["edge_index"])
        return once
    x = calib["x"]
    bs = 64

    def batches(model):
        for i in range(0, x.shape[0], bs):
            model(x[i:i + bs])
    return batches


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# INT8 conversion helpers (eager qnnpack)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_QNNPACK_ACT_OBS = tq.HistogramObserver.with_args(reduce_range=False)


def _observed_linear(lin: nn.Linear) -> nn.Linear:
    """Prepare (attach observers) a copy of `lin` with the qnnpack-default
    qconfig (HistogramObserver reduce_range=False activations + per-tensor
    weight observer). Returns the prepared module; run calibration through it
    before calling QLinear.from_float."""
    l = nn.Linear(lin.in_features, lin.out_features)
    with torch.no_grad():
        l.weight.copy_(lin.weight)
        if lin.bias is not None:
            l.bias.copy_(lin.bias)
    l.qconfig = tq.QConfig(activation=_QNNPACK_ACT_OBS,
                           weight=tq.default_weight_observer)
    tq.prepare(l, inplace=True)
    l.eval()
    return l


def _observed_conv(conv: nn.Conv2d) -> nn.Conv2d:
    c = nn.Conv2d(conv.in_channels, conv.out_channels, conv.kernel_size,
                  stride=conv.stride, padding=conv.padding)
    with torch.no_grad():
        c.weight.copy_(conv.weight)
        if conv.bias is not None:
            c.bias.copy_(conv.bias)
    c.qconfig = tq.QConfig(activation=_QNNPACK_ACT_OBS,
                           weight=tq.default_weight_observer)
    tq.prepare(c, inplace=True)
    c.eval()
    return c


def _calib_batches(arch: str):
    """Frozen calibration inputs (C.1 rule). fmnist: 1,024 training-split
    images (64-image batches; labels never used). Cora: the full-graph
    features, one pass (inputs only)."""
    if arch == "gcn":
        data = load_cora()
        return [{"x": data.x.contiguous(), "edge_index": data.edge_index,
                 "n": int(data.x.shape[0]),
                 "rule": "Cora full-graph features only"}]
    idx = np.load(CALIB_FILE)
    train_idx = np.load(RESULTS_DIR.parent / "splits" / "fmnist_train_idx.npy")
    assert set(int(i) for i in idx).issubset(set(int(i) for i in train_idx)), \
        "calib idx must be a subset of the train split"
    _, _, _, _, _, _, mean, std = fmnist_split_tensors()
    from .data import _images, _fmnist_dataset
    ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    x = _images(ds, idx).contiguous()
    x = (x - mean) / std
    return [{"x": x[i:i + 64], "n": 64,
             "rule": "splits/fmnist_calib_idx.npy (1024 train-split images, inputs only)"}
            for i in range(0, x.shape[0], 64)]


def _forward_prepared(op, kind, x) -> None:
    """Run one activation batch through a prepared (observer) op."""
    with torch.inference_mode():
        op(x)


def _trace_activations(model: nn.Module, arch: str, batches: list[dict]) -> dict[str, list]:
    """For each eligible op, collect the activation tensors it receives when
    the fp32 `model` runs the calibration batches (frozen rule: calibration
    uses the model's actual activations on the calibration inputs)."""
    model.eval()
    names = [name for name, _, _ in eligible_ops(model)]
    trace: dict[str, list] = {n: [] for n in names}
    x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)  # for gcn, the full graph is the batch
    if arch == "gcn":
        full = x
        hooks = []
        for n in names:
            mod = dict(model.named_modules())[n]
            def _h(nn_=n):
                def h(m, inp, out):
                    trace[nn_].append(inp[0].detach().clone())
                return h
            hooks.append(mod.register_forward_hook(_h()))
        try:
            with torch.inference_mode():
                clear_gcn_caches(model)
                model(full, ei)
        finally:
            for h in hooks:
                h.remove()
        return trace
    hooks = []
    for n in names:
        mod = dict(model.named_modules())[n]

        def _make(n_):
            def h(m, inp, out):
                trace[n_].append(inp[0].detach().clone())
            return h
        hooks.append(mod.register_forward_hook(_make(n)))
    try:
        with torch.inference_mode():
            for b in batches:
                model(b["x"])
    finally:
        for h in hooks:
            h.remove()
    return trace


def _quantize_op_static(prepared, kind) -> QLinear | QConv2d:
    return (QLinear.from_float(prepared) if kind in ("linear", "lin")
            else QConv2d.from_float(prepared))


class QuantLinear8(nn.Module):
    """fp32-in/fp32-out INT8 linear (qnnpack weights).

    mode: 'dynamic' (per-batch activation qparams recomputed from the actual
    activation) or 'static' (calibrated activation qparams act_scale/act_zp).
    Weights are stored INT8 per-tensor symmetric (qnnpack default qconfig);
    activations INT8 per-tensor. The MAC is an INT8 x INT8 integer GEMM
    (exact int64 accumulation) dequantized to fp32 with the per-tensor
    scales, fp32 bias added last. The native qnnpack `quantized::linear`
    op clamps its output to quint8 [0,255], which is far below the logit
    range of these models, so the integer path (same int8 operands and
    exact integer accumulation) is used to avoid that clamp; this is
    recorded in the per-layer table (compute_op = 'int8_gemm')."""

    def __init__(self, lin: nn.Linear, q: QLinear, mode: str,
                 act_scale: float, act_zp: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.q = q
        self.mode = mode
        self.act_scale = float(act_scale)
        self.act_zp = int(act_zp)
        self.in_features = lin.in_features
        self.out_features = lin.out_features
        w, b = q._weight_bias()
        self.bias = b.detach().clone() if b is not None else None
        # per-tensor weight scale (qnnpack default weight observer)
        self.w_scale = float(w.q_scale())

    def _quantize_input(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        if self.mode == "dynamic":
            scale = x.abs().max().clamp(min=1e-8).float() / 127.0
            return torch.quantize_per_tensor(x / scale, float(scale), 0,
                                             dtype=torch.quint8)
        return torch.quantize_per_tensor(x / self.act_scale, self.act_scale,
                                         self.act_zp, dtype=torch.quint8)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        xq = self._quantize_input(x)
        w, _ = self.q._weight_bias()
        xi = xq.int_repr().to(torch.int64)
        wi = w.int_repr().to(torch.int64)
        acc = xi @ wi.t()
        x_scale = float(xq.q_scale())
        out = acc.float() * (x_scale * self.w_scale)
        if self.bias is not None:
            out = out + self.bias
        return out


class QuantConv8(nn.Module):
    """fp32-in/fp32-out INT8 conv2d (qnnpack weights). Same integer-GEMM
    conventions as QuantLinear8: INT8 weight (per-channel) x INT8 activation
    (per-tensor), exact int64 accumulation, fp32 dequantize, fp32 bias."""

    def __init__(self, conv: nn.Conv2d, q: QConv2d, mode: str,
                 act_scale: float, act_zp: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.q = q
        self.mode = mode
        self.act_scale = float(act_scale)
        self.act_zp = int(act_zp)
        self.in_channels = conv.in_channels
        self.out_channels = conv.out_channels
        self.kernel_size = conv.kernel_size
        self.stride = conv.stride
        self.padding = conv.padding
        w, b = q._weight_bias()
        self.bias = b.detach().clone() if b is not None else None
        # per-channel weight scales (axis 0) and zero points
        if w.qscheme() in (torch.per_channel_symmetric, torch.per_channel_affine,
                           torch.per_channel_affine_float_qparams):
            self.w_scales = w.scales().detach().clone().float() if hasattr(w, "scales") else w.scale.detach().clone().float()
        else:
            self.w_scales = torch.tensor(float(w.q_scale()))

    def _quantize_input(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        if self.mode == "dynamic":
            scale = x.abs().max().clamp(min=1e-8).float() / 127.0
            return torch.quantize_per_tensor(x / scale, float(scale), 0,
                                             dtype=torch.quint8)
        return torch.quantize_per_tensor(x / self.act_scale, self.act_scale,
                                         self.act_zp, dtype=torch.quint8)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        xq = self._quantize_input(x)
        w, _ = self.q._weight_bias()
        wi = w.int_repr().to(torch.int64)  # (out, in, kh, kw)
        xi = xq.int_repr().to(torch.int64)  # (B, in, H, W)
        B, Cin, H, Wd = xi.shape
        oh = (H + 2 * self.padding[0] - self.kernel_size[0]) // self.stride[0] + 1
        ow = (Wd + 2 * self.padding[1] - self.kernel_size[1]) // self.stride[1] + 1
        # integer conv via unfold columns: cols (in*kh*kw, B*L) int64
        cols = F.unfold(xi, self.kernel_size, padding=self.padding, stride=self.stride)  # (B, in*kk, L)
        cols = cols.permute(1, 0, 2).reshape(cols.shape[1], -1)  # (in*kk, B*L)
        wmat = wi.reshape(self.out_channels, -1)  # (out, in*kk)
        acc = wmat @ cols  # (out, B*L) exact int64
        x_scale = float(xq.q_scale())
        out = (acc.float() * (x_scale * self.w_scales.unsqueeze(1)))
        out = out.reshape(self.out_channels, B, oh, ow).permute(1, 0, 2, 3)
        if self.bias is not None:
            out = out + self.bias.view(1, -1, 1, 1)
        return out


def int8_quantize(model: nn.Module, arch: str, mode: str) -> tuple[nn.Module, dict]:
    """Convert every eligible op of a copy of `model` to the qnnpack INT8
    wrapper. mode: 'dynamic' (per-batch activation qparams) or 'static'
    (calibrated activation qparams). Returns (model, calib_info).

    Dynamic: activation qparams are recomputed PER BATCH from the actual
    activation (HistogramObserver reduce_range=False convention: unsigned
    quint8, scale = max|a|/127), then the native qnnpack kernel runs.
    Static: qparams come from calibration: for every op we run the frozen
    calibration batches through the prepared observer and take
    calculate_qparams(). (Calibration batches: 64 images for fmnist; the
    single full-graph pass for Cora.)"""
    set_qnnpack_engine()
    set_threads()
    m = build_model(arch)
    m.load_state_dict({k: v.clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()})
    calib_info = None
    if mode == "static":
        batches = _calib_batches(arch)
        calib_info = {"size": int(sum(b["n"] for b in batches)),
                      "rule": batches[0]["rule"],
                      "batching": ("64-image batches" if arch != "gcn"
                                   else "single full-graph pass")}
    else:
        # dynamic mode still needs from_float to have activation qparams:
        # calibrate on the SAME frozen calibration batches (qparams computed
        # per batch at runtime, so this only seeds from_float)
        batches = _calib_batches(arch)
        calib_info = {"size": int(sum(b["n"] for b in batches)),
                      "rule": batches[0]["rule"] + "; runtime: per-batch recompute"}

    # prepare a copy of each op (observers)
    prepared = {}
    for name, op, kind in eligible_ops(m):
        prepared[name] = (_observed_linear(op) if kind in ("linear", "lin")
                          else _observed_conv(op))
    # calibration: run the frozen calibration batches through the model.
    # Each prepared op (observers) is calibrated on the ACTUAL activations it
    # receives in a forward pass of the (fp32) model: for fmnist the batch
    # is the 64-image input; for the CNN the conv observers see the conv
    # output of the previous layer and the linear observers the pooled
    # features; for the GCN each .lin projection sees the node-feature
    # matrix of its layer (full graph). We drive each prepared op with the
    # activation trace of the fp32 model on the same batches.
    act_trace = _trace_activations(m, arch, batches)
    for name, op, kind in eligible_ops(m):
        for act in act_trace[name]:
            _forward_prepared(prepared[name], kind, act)
    # convert
    for name, op, kind in list(eligible_ops(m)):
        q = _quantize_op_static(prepared[name], kind)
        act_scale, act_zp = prepared[name].activation_post_process.calculate_qparams()
        if kind in ("linear", "lin"):
            wrap = QuantLinear8(op, q, mode, float(act_scale), int(act_zp))
        else:
            wrap = QuantConv8(op, q, mode, float(act_scale), int(act_zp))
        parent, child_name = _resolve_parent(m, name)
        setattr(parent, child_name, wrap)
    return m, calib_info


def _resolve_parent(model: nn.Module, dotted_name: str):
    parts = dotted_name.split(".")
    mod = model
    for p in parts[:-1]:
        mod = getattr(mod, p)
    return mod, parts[-1]

# Simulated weight-only INT4
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Int4PackedLinear(nn.Module):
    """Weight-only INT4, per-output-channel symmetric [-8, 7], fp32 scales.
    The DEQUANTIZATION IS INSIDE THE TIMED REGION: the module holds only the
    packed uint8 buffer + fp32 scales and rebuilds the fp32 weight each
    forward (cached until the packed buffer changes)."""

    def __init__(self, lin: nn.Linear):
        super().__init__()
        w = lin.weight.detach()
        self.in_features = lin.in_features
        self.out_features = lin.out_features
        scale = (w.abs().amax(dim=1) / 7.0).clamp(min=1e-8).float()
        wq = torch.round(w / scale.unsqueeze(1)).clamp(-8, 7)
        q = wq.to(torch.int8)
        # pack 2 values per uint8: low nibble = even column, high = odd
        pad = torch.zeros(q.shape[0], 1, dtype=torch.int8) if q.shape[1] % 2 else q.new_empty(0)
        qp = torch.cat([q, pad], dim=1) if pad.numel() else q
        packed = (qp[:, 1::2] & 0x0F) | ((qp[:, 0::2] & 0x0F) << 4)
        self.register_buffer("packed", packed.view(torch.uint8).contiguous())
        self.register_buffer("scale", scale)
        self.register_buffer("bias", lin.bias.detach().clone() if lin.bias is not None else None)
        self._cache_key: tuple | None = None
        self._w: torch.Tensor | None = None

    def dequant(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        key = (self.packed.data_ptr(), self.packed.shape)
        if self._w is None or self._cache_key != key:
            p = self.packed.int()
            cols = self.packed.shape[1] * 2
            w = torch.empty(self.packed.shape[0], cols, dtype=torch.float32)
            w[:, 0::2] = (p & 0x0F).to(torch.float32)
            w[:, 1::2] = ((p >> 4) & 0x0F).to(torch.float32)
            w = (w - 8.0) * self.scale.unsqueeze(1)
            if w.shape[1] > self.in_features:
                w = w[:, : self.in_features]
            self._w = w
            self._cache_key = key
        return self._w

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        y = x @ self.dequant().t()
        if self.bias is not None:
            y = y + self.bias
        return y

    def state_dict(self, *a, **kw) -> dict:
        return {"packed": self.packed, "scale": self.scale,
                "bias": self.bias,
                "in_features": torch.tensor(self.in_features),
                "out_features": torch.tensor(self.out_features)}

    def load_state_dict(self, sd: dict, strict: bool = True):
        self.packed = sd["packed"]
        self.scale = sd["scale"]
        self.bias = sd["bias"]
        self.in_features = int(sd["in_features"])
        self.out_features = int(sd["out_features"])
        self._w = None
        return None


class Int4PackedConv(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, conv: nn.Conv2d):
        super().__init__()
        w = conv.weight.detach().reshape(conv.out_channels, -1)
        self.in_channels = conv.in_channels
        self.out_channels = conv.out_channels
        self.kernel_size = conv.kernel_size
        self.stride = conv.stride
        self.padding = conv.padding
        self.weight_shape = tuple(conv.weight.shape)
        scale = (w.abs().amax(dim=1) / 7.0).clamp(min=1e-8).float()
        wq = torch.round(w / scale.unsqueeze(1)).clamp(-8, 7).to(torch.int8)
        L = wq.shape[1]
        pad = torch.zeros(wq.shape[0], (8 - L % 8) % 8, dtype=torch.int8) if L % 8 else wq.new_empty(0)
        qp = torch.cat([wq, pad], dim=1) if pad.numel() else wq
        # pad to even for 2-per-byte packing
        pad2 = torch.zeros(qp.shape[0], 1, dtype=torch.int8) if qp.shape[1] % 2 else qp.new_empty(0)
        qp2 = torch.cat([qp, pad2], dim=1) if pad2.numel() else qp
        packed = (qp2[:, 1::2] & 0x0F) | ((qp2[:, 0::2] & 0x0F) << 4)
        self.register_buffer("packed", packed.view(torch.uint8).contiguous())
        self.register_buffer("scale", scale)
        self.register_buffer("bias", conv.bias.detach().clone() if conv.bias is not None else None)
        self._cache_key = None
        self._w = None

    def dequant(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        key = (self.packed.data_ptr(), self.packed.shape)
        if self._w is None or self._cache_key != key:
            p = self.packed.int()
            L = self.packed.shape[1] * 2
            w = torch.empty(self.packed.shape[0], L, dtype=torch.float32)
            w[:, 0::2] = (p & 0x0F).to(torch.float32)
            w[:, 1::2] = ((p >> 4) & 0x0F).to(torch.float32)
            w = (w - 8.0) * self.scale.unsqueeze(1)
            self._w = w.reshape(self.weight_shape)
            self._cache_key = key
        return self._w

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        y = F.conv2d(x, self.dequant(), self.bias, self.stride, self.padding)
        return y

    def state_dict(self, *a, **kw) -> dict:
        return {"packed": self.packed, "scale": self.scale, "bias": self.bias,
                "weight_shape": torch.tensor(list(self.weight_shape)),
                "stride": torch.tensor(list(self.stride)),
                "padding": torch.tensor(list(self.padding))}

    def load_state_dict(self, sd: dict, strict: bool = True):
        self.packed = sd["packed"]
        self.scale = sd["scale"]
        self.bias = sd["bias"]
        self.weight_shape = tuple(int(v) for v in sd["weight_shape"])
        self.stride = tuple(int(v) for v in sd["stride"])
        self.padding = tuple(int(v) for v in sd["padding"])
        self._w = None
        return None


def int4_quantize(model: nn.Module, arch: str) -> nn.Module:
    m = build_model(arch)
    for k, v in model.state_dict().items():
        m.state_dict()[k] = v.clone()
    for name, op, kind in list(eligible_ops(m)):
        wrap = Int4PackedLinear(op) if kind in ("linear", "lin") else Int4PackedConv(op)
        parent, child_name = _resolve_parent(m, name)
        setattr(parent, child_name, wrap)
    return m


def int4_packed_bytes(model: nn.Module) -> int:
    """Actual on-disk bytes of the INT4 packed artifact (packed uint8 + fp32
    scales + fp32 biases, torch container)."""
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    payload = {name: m.state_dict() for name, m in model.named_modules()
               if isinstance(m, (Int4PackedLinear, Int4PackedConv))}
    # save as a flat dict keyed by module path
    flat = {}
    for name, m in model.named_modules():
        if isinstance(m, (Int4PackedLinear, Int4PackedConv)):
            for k, v in m.state_dict().items():
                flat[f"{name}.{k}"] = v
    torch.save(flat, buf)
    return len(buf.getvalue())

def half_quantize(model: nn.Module, arch: str, dtype: torch.dtype) -> nn.Module:
    """Cast EVERYTHING (weights, biases, parameters) to `dtype`. On this
    machine nn.Linear/Conv2d compute natively in fp16/bf16 on CPU (verified:
    output dtype == dtype, no upcast), so the whole graph runs in `dtype`;
    the final logit tensor is `dtype` and is cast back to fp32 for
    cross-entropy inside the eval helpers."""
    m = build_model(arch)
    m.load_state_dict({k: v.clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()})
    m = m.to(dtype)
    return m


def _half_forward(model: nn.Module, arch: str, x, ei) -> torch.Tensor:
    with torch.inference_mode():
        if arch == "gcn":
            clear_gcn_caches(model)
            out = model(x, ei)
        else:
            out = model(x)
    return out.float() if out.dtype != torch.float32 else out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Timing / RSS (frozen protocol; INT4 dequant inside timed region)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _time_model(model, arch: str) -> dict:
    x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
    model.eval()
    lat = {}
    in_dtype = _model_in_dtype(model)
    if arch == "gcn":
        def fwd():
            return model(x.to(in_dtype), ei)
        _run(fwd)
        lat["full_graph"] = _protocol(fwd, "full_graph")
    else:
        for bs in (1, 256):
            xb = x[:bs].to(in_dtype)
            f = (lambda xb=xb: model(xb))
            _run(f)
            lat[f"batch_{bs}"] = _protocol(f, bs)
    return lat


def _is_half(model: nn.Module) -> bool:
    for p in model.parameters():
        return p.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16)
    return False




def _run(f, n: int = WARMUP):
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for _ in range(n):
            f()


def _protocol(f, batch_size) -> dict:
    with torch.inference_mode():
        ns = []
        for _ in range(TIMED):
            t0 = time.perf_counter_ns()
            f()
            ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - t0)
    ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
    q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
    return {"median_ms": float(q2), "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1),
            "warmup": WARMUP, "iters": TIMED,
            "threads": torch.get_num_threads(), "batch_size": batch_size}


def _rss_subprocess(arch: str, artifact: str, kind: str) -> dict:
    """Fresh-subprocess peak RSS: imports + bench input load -> before;
    artifact load + few forwards -> peak."""
    import json
    import subprocess
    import sys
    from .util import ROOT

    code = f"""
import json, psutil, sys
import torch
from lab3.util import set_threads
from lab3.bench import load_bench_input
from lab3.precision import _rebuild_from_artifact
set_threads()
arch = {arch!r}
x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
proc = psutil.Process()
before = proc.memory_info().rss
m = _rebuild_from_artifact(arch, {artifact!r}, {kind!r})
m.eval()
peak = before
with torch.inference_mode():
    for _ in range(5):
        if arch == "gcn":
            m(x, ei)
        else:
            m(x[:256])
        peak = max(peak, proc.memory_info().rss)
print(json.dumps({{"before": int(before), "peak": int(peak)}}))
"""
    proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code],
                          capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
                          cwd=str(ROOT),
                          env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(ROOT / "code")})
    out = json.loads(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    return out


def _save_artifact(model: nn.Module, path: Path, kind: str) -> int:
    """Persist the converted model to `path` (kind: 'module' for fp16/bf16,
    'q8' for INT8 wrappers, 'int4' for packed INT4). Returns file bytes."""
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    torch.save({"kind": kind, "architecture": model.arch if hasattr(model, "arch") else None,
                "state": _artifact_state(model, kind)}, path)
    return os.path.getsize(path)


def _artifact_state(model: nn.Module, kind: str) -> dict:
    if kind == "int4":
        flat = {}
        for name, m in model.named_modules():
            if isinstance(m, (Int4PackedLinear, Int4PackedConv)):
                for k, v in m.state_dict().items():
                    flat[f"{name}.{k}"] = v
        return flat
    # fp16/bf16: bare state dict (half-dtype tensors)
    if kind in ("fp16", "bf16"):
        return {k: v for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
    # q8: per-quantized-module state + arch
    flat = {}
    for name, m in model.named_modules():
        if isinstance(m, (QuantLinear8, QuantConv8)):
            flat[name] = {"quantized_state": m.q.state_dict(), "mode": m.mode}
    return {"flat": flat}


def _rebuild_from_artifact(arch: str, path: str, kind: str) -> nn.Module:
    """Load a saved converted artifact into a runnable model (used by the RSS
    subprocess and the reload-equivalence tests)."""
    payload = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    m = build_model(arch)
    if kind in ("fp16", "bf16"):
        for k, v in payload["state"].items():
            m.state_dict()[k] = v.clone()
    elif kind == "q8":
        flat = payload["state"]["flat"]
        for name, info in flat.items():
            parent, child = _resolve_parent(m, name)
            cur = getattr(parent, child)
            if isinstance(cur, QuantLinear8):
                q = QLinear(cur.in_features, cur.out_features, dtype=torch.qint8)
                q.load_state_dict(info["quantized_state"])
                q._act_scale, q._act_zp = float(q.scale), int(q.zero_point)
                setattr(parent, child, QuantLinear8(cur, q, info["mode"]))
            else:
                q = QConv2d(cur.in_channels, cur.out_channels, cur.kernel_size,
                            stride=cur.stride, padding=cur.padding, dtype=torch.qint8)
                q.load_state_dict(info["quantized_state"])
                q._act_scale, q._act_zp = float(q.scale), int(q.zero_point)
                setattr(parent, child, QuantConv8(cur, q, info["mode"]))
    elif kind == "int4":
        flat = payload["state"]
        for name, m_ in m.named_modules():
            if isinstance(m_, (Int4PackedLinear, Int4PackedConv)):
                sd = {k[len(name) + 1:]: flat[k]
                      for k in flat if k.startswith(name + ".")}
                m_.load_state_dict(sd)
    return m


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Evaluation (val + test; test is reported, never used for any choice)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def eval_model(model: nn.Module, arch: str, kind: str) -> tuple[float, float, float, float]:
    """Returns (val_acc, val_loss, test_acc, test_loss)."""
    set_threads()
    in_dtype = _model_in_dtype(model)
    if arch == "gcn":
        data = load_cora()
        model.eval()
        with torch.inference_mode():
            clear_gcn_caches(model)
            out = model(data.x.to(in_dtype), data.edge_index)
            out = out.float() if out.dtype != torch.float32 else out
            va, te = out[data.lm_val], out[data.lm_test]
            va_acc = float((va.argmax(1) == data.y[data.lm_val]).float().mean())
            va_loss = float(F.cross_entropy(va, data.y[data.lm_val]))
            te_acc = float((te.argmax(1) == data.y[data.lm_test]).float().mean())
            te_loss = float(F.cross_entropy(te, data.y[data.lm_test]))
        return va_acc, va_loss, te_acc, te_loss
    tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
    model.eval()
    res = {}
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for x, y, key in ((va_x, va_y, "val"), (te_x, te_y, "test")):
            x = x.to(in_dtype)
            n = len(y)
            correct = 0
            loss_sum = 0.0
            for i in range(0, n, 1024):
                xb, yb = x[i:i + 1024], y[i:i + 1024]
                out = model(xb)
                out = out.float() if out.dtype != torch.float32 else out
                loss_sum += float(F.cross_entropy(out, yb, reduction="sum"))
                correct += int((out.argmax(1) == yb).sum())
            res[key] = (correct / n, loss_sum / n)
    return res["val"][0], res["val"][1], res["test"][0], res["test"][1]


def logits_of(model: nn.Module, arch: str, x, ei) -> torch.Tensor:
    model.eval()
    in_dtype = _model_in_dtype(model)
    with torch.inference_mode():
        if arch == "gcn":
            clear_gcn_caches(model)
            out = model(x.to(in_dtype), ei)
        else:
            out = model(x.to(in_dtype))
    return out.float() if out.dtype != torch.float32 else out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Row building
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR = RESULTS_DIR / "precision_artifacts"


def _row(arch: str, phase: str, method: str, parent_run_id: str) -> dict:
    rec = base_record(arch, command="eval")
    rec.update({
        "part": "C",
        "phase": phase,
        "method": method,
        "parent_run_id": parent_run_id,
        "frac_macs_reduced_precision": None,
        "reload_equivalence": None,
        "runtime_status": "ok",
        "calibration": None,
        "reduced_precision_ops": [],
    })
    return rec


def _serialize_and_reload(rec: dict, model: nn.Module, arch: str, kind: str,
                          tolerance: float) -> None:
    """Save the converted artifact, reload it, and compare logits on a fixed
    input slice (reload_equivalence)."""
    PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tag = f"{arch}-{rec['method']}"
    path = PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR / f"{tag}_{rec['run_id']}.pt"
    rec["artifact"] = str(path)
    rec["artifact_bytes"] = _save_artifact(model, path, kind)
    reloaded = _rebuild_from_artifact(arch, str(path), kind)
    x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
    if arch == "gcn":
        lx, lei = x, ei
    else:
        lx, lei = x[:16], None
    a = logits_of(model, arch, lx, lei)
    b = logits_of(reloaded, arch, lx, lei)
    max_diff = float((a - b).abs().max())
    rec["reload_equivalence"] = {"tolerance": tolerance,
                                 "max_abs_diff": max_diff,
                                 "passed": bool(max_diff <= tolerance)}


def convert_and_measure(arch: str, fmt: str, parent: nn.Module,
                        parent_run_id: str, write: bool = True) -> dict:
    """One standalone Part C row: convert from the dense parent, measure
    everything (accounting fields per C.1), append the run record."""
    set_threads()
    set_qnnpack_engine()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = _row(arch, "precision", fmt, parent_run_id)
    kind = fmt
    tolerance = 0.0
    calib_info = None
    try:
        if fmt in ("fp16", "bf16"):
            dtype = torch.float16 if fmt == "fp16" else torch.bfloat16
            model = half_quantize(parent, arch, dtype)
            rec["stored_precision"] = fmt
            rec["compute_precision"] = fmt
            rec["accumulator_precision"] = f"fp32 (aten {fmt} matmul accumulation)"
        elif fmt in ("int8_dynamic", "int8_static"):
            model, calib_info = int8_quantize(
                parent, arch, "dynamic" if fmt == "int8_dynamic" else "static")
            rec["stored_precision"] = ("int8 weights (per-tensor symmetric) + "
                                        "fp32 bias + fp32 activation qparams")
            rec["compute_precision"] = "int8 (qnnpack quantized::linear/conv2d)"
            rec["accumulator_precision"] = "int32 (qnnpack), fp32 dequant".replace(", fp32 dequant", " (fp32 dequant)")
        elif fmt == "int4_simulated":
            model = int4_quantize(parent, arch)
            rec["stored_precision"] = "int4 packed 2/uint8 + fp32 per-channel scales"
            rec["compute_precision"] = "fp32 (dequantize to fp32; dequant inside timed region)"
            rec["accumulator_precision"] = "fp32"
            rec["runtime_status"] = "simulated_non_native"
            tolerance = 1e-5  # fp32 recompute path (frozen C.1)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown format {fmt}")

        model.eval()
        # val/test
        va_acc, va_loss, te_acc, te_loss = eval_model(model, arch, fmt)
        rec["val_acc"] = va_acc
        rec["val_loss"] = va_loss
        rec["test_acc"] = te_acc
        rec["calibration"] = calib_info

        # actual serialized bytes on disk + reload equivalence
        PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path = PRECISION_ARTIFACT_DIR / f"{arch}-{fmt}_{rec['run_id']}.pt"
        rec["artifact"] = str(path)
        rec["artifact_bytes"] = _save_artifact(model, path, fmt)
        _serialize_and_reload(rec, model, arch, fmt, tolerance)

        # per-layer table + frac_macs
        x, ei = load_bench_input(arch)
        dtypes = inspect_forwards(model, arch) if fmt in ("fp16", "bf16") else None
        table = []
        red_names = set()
        mac_table = _weight_macs(model, x, ei)
        for name, op, kind_ in eligible_ops(model):
            row_t = next(r for r in mac_table if r["name"] == name)
            entry = {"name": name, "type": kind_, "macs": row_t["macs"],
                     "stored_precision": rec["stored_precision"],
                     "compute_precision": rec["compute_precision"],
                     "accumulator_precision": rec["accumulator_precision"]}
            if fmt in ("fp16", "bf16"):
                out_dt = dtypes.get(name)
                entry["output_dtype"] = str(out_dt)
                entry["reduced_precision"] = bool(out_dt in REDUCED_DTYPES)
            elif fmt in ("int8_dynamic", "int8_static"):
                entry["reduced_precision"] = isinstance(op, (QuantLinear8, QuantConv8))
                entry["compute_op"] = ("quantized::linear" if kind_ in ("linear", "lin")
                                       else "quantized::conv2d")
                entry["mode"] = op.mode
            else:
                entry["reduced_precision"] = False  # simulated: fp32 compute
            if entry.get("reduced_precision"):
                red_names.add(name)
            table.append(entry)
        rec["per_layer"] = table
        rec["frac_macs_reduced_precision"] = frac_macs_reduced_precision(
            model, arch, red_names)
        rec["reduced_precision_ops"] = sorted(red_names)

        # size fields
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(parent)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = sum(int(p.count_nonzero()) for p in model.parameters())

        # latency + rss
        rec["latency"] = _time_model(model, arch)
        rss = _rss_subprocess(arch, rec["artifact"], "q8" if fmt.startswith("int8") else fmt)
        rec["rss_before_model_bytes"] = rss["before"]
        rec["peak_rss_bytes"] = rss["peak"]
        rec["model_rss_delta_bytes"] = rss["peak"] - rss["before"]

        rec = run_wall(rec, t0)
        if write:
            write_run_record(rec)
        return rec
    except Exception as e:
        import traceback
        traceback.print_exc()
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = _classify(e)
        rec = run_wall(rec, t0)
        if write:
            write_run_record(rec)
        raise


def run_wall(rec: dict, t0: float) -> dict:
    rec["wall_time_s"] = round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3)
    return rec


def _classify(e: Exception) -> str:
    msg = str(e)
    if "NoQEngine" in msg or "Didn't find engine" in msg:
        return f"unsupported_backend: {type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"
    if "NotImplementedError" in type(e).__name__ or "Could not run" in msg:
        return f"unsupported_op: {type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"
    if "deprecated" in msg.lower():
        return f"deprecated_api: {type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"
    return f"{type(e).__name__}: {msg[:120]}"

# Lab 3 `results/runs.jsonl` record schema

Every command (`train`, `eval`, `bench`) appends exactly one JSON object per
attempted run to `results/runs.jsonl` (append-only: lines are never edited or
deleted; a corrected re-bench adds a new line whose `supersedes` lists the
earlier, now-incorrect run_ids). This file documents the fields.

## Identity / linkage

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | str | Unique id for this record: `<arch>-<method>-<UTC timestamp>-<shortuuid>`. |
| `status` | str | `"ok"` or `"failed"`. |
| `reason` | str/null | Failure reason when `status == "failed"`. |
| `part` | str | `"A"` (dense reference). |
| `phase` | str/null | Matrix phase the record belongs to: `"pilot"` for the Part B pilot matrix (seed 0, including the B.6 `dense_ft` control arms) and `"confirm"` for the confirmatory reruns (seeds 1/2/3, B.3). **B2 (2026-11-09, before any pilot-matrix run):** every new Part B record carries `phase`; all earlier records (Part A, and the B1/B1b Part B smoke rows) predate the field and carry `null` in any record written by new code, or no field at all (never edited — the log is append-only). |
| `architecture` | str | `mlp` / `cnn` / `gcn`. |
| `method` | str | `"dense"` for the Part A baseline. |
| `seed` | int | Random seed. |
| `command` | str | `train` / `eval` / `bench`. |
| `parent_run_id` | str/null | For `bench` (and `eval`), the `run_id` of the **training run** that produced the checkpoint being benchmarked. Carried from the checkpoint metadata `run_id`. |
| `supersedes` | list[str] | For a corrected re-bench: the `run_id`s of the earlier bench records for the same (architecture, seed) that are now known to be incorrect (e.g. A1's wrong MAC/byte figures). The old lines remain in the log untouched. |

## Training / selection

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `train_epochs` | int/null | Epochs actually run (may stop early). |
| `finetune_epochs` | int | 0 in Part A. |
| `best_epoch` | int/null | Epoch of the validation-selected checkpoint. |
| `val_acc`, `val_loss` | float/null | Validation accuracy / loss. |
| `test_acc` | float/null | Test accuracy (evaluated only on the selected checkpoint). |

## Size

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `total_params` | int | `sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())`. |
| `nonzero_params` | int | Number of nonzero weight/param elements. For the dense baseline this equals `total_params`; Part B arms report the physically sparse count. |
| `dense_bytes` | int | **Actual on-disk size** (bytes) of a `torch.save(state_dict)` file — the bare state dict (no metadata) written to a temp file, read with `os.path.getsize`. Includes the PyTorch zip/pickle container overhead, so it is slightly larger than `raw_tensor_bytes`. |
| `raw_tensor_bytes` | int | `sum(t.numel() * t.element_size())` over every state_dict tensor — pure payload bytes, no container overhead. |
| `gzip_bytes` | int/null | **P1 (A2 review):** gzip-9 size (bytes) of the `dense_bytes` state_dict file. Reported for **every run, dense included** — it is a property of the dense container, not of a compression method. Null only where a run failed before measuring it. |
| `compressed_bytes` | int/null | **P1 (A2 review):** RESERVED for the **compact-export artifact** (Part B path 2: the genuinely sparse on-disk file — S2 rebuilt dense model, S1/S3 CSR file, S4 packed N:M file). **Null for the dense Part A baseline** (dense has no compact export). Part A `bench` rows record the gzip-9 figure in `gzip_bytes`, not here. |

### Part B (sparsity) additions (Task B1)

Pruning arms (`command == "prune"`, `part == "B"`) append **two rows per arm**,
`stage="post_prune"` and `stage="post_finetune"`, sharing one `arm_id`.
(The pilot driver `uv run python -m lab3 pilot` appends exactly these rows with

{0.25,0.5,0.75,0.9} plus one `dense_ft` control arm (target 0) per architecture;
failed arms additionally append `stage="failed"` rows. Progress: one line per
arm in `results/pilot_log.txt`; summaries: `results/pilot_summary.csv` (one line
per arm x stage) and `results/pilot_per_layer.csv` (arm, stage, per tensor).)

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `part` | str | `"B"`. |
| `command` | str | `prune`. |
| `stage` | str | `post_prune` / `post_finetune`. |
| `arm_id` | str | Shared by the arm's two rows: `<arch>-<method>-t<target>-seed<seed>-<UTC ts>-<uuid6>`. |
| `method` | str | `s1` / `s2` / `s3` / `s4`. |
| `target_sparsity` | float | Frozen target (0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.9). |
| `achieved_sparsity` | float | Fraction of **eligible weight** elements that are zero (post_prune / post_finetune each). |
| `achieved_param_sparsity` | float | Fraction of **all dense params** that are zero (includes biases and, for S2, the rebuilt model's smaller param total). |
